FIVE INDIVIDUAL FLAGSHIP RESEARCH CONTRACTS F121 / Quantum-Chemical Simulation of Aroma Electronic Structure at the Limit The proposed physical object is electronic-structure prediction of authenticated botanical odorant molecules, with emphasis on electron correlation, density functional approximation, basis-set incompleteness, spin state, reference geometry, stereochemistry, pseudopotential choice and convergence diagnostics. Primary decision: Electronic structure energy MAE [kJ/mol]. The minimum reproducible prototype needs digitally identified terpene molecular graphs, stereochemical identifiers, reproducible geometries and frozen quantum chemistry input files. Compare to same-geometry high-level classical quantum chemistry, where feasible DLPNO-CCSD(T) or carefully converged reference calculations under a registered resource budget. An independent observer must evaluate independently generated matched-geometry high-level electronic-energy tables with computational settings, provenance and uncertainty. Blinded adversarial intervention: blinded stereoisomer-label permutation with a concealed basis-set and geometry swap. Potentially stronger rival: conformer omission, changed reference geometry or inconsistent electronic reference state rather than an improved Hamiltonian approximation. Hard stop: missing independent energy reference, uncontrolled charge or spin, nonconvergent SCF or undisclosed multi-reference character. This is a research-design contract, not a newly verified gain. Successor interpretation: model, molecular identity, reference and reported uncertainty travel together. No favorable synthetic numerical residual should be substituted for a molecule-specific converged quantum calculation. In F121, the strongest classical analysis may win. Preserve all unsuccessful inputs, problematic spin or photochemical states and withheld counterexamples. A research gate is an invitation to reject the model when evidence requires it. F122 / Conformational Energy Landscapes of Botanical Terpenes at the Limit The proposed physical object is ranking of torsional conformers in complex botanical terpene stereoisomers, with emphasis on torsional potential energy, conformer search coverage, Boltzmann populations, thermal barriers, stereo- and enantiomer assignment, correlated energy errors and duplicated minima. Primary decision: Conformer rank agreement (Kendall tau) [ratio]. The minimum reproducible prototype needs authenticated cis/trans and enantiomeric terpene structures, archived conformer search seeds and blinded reference-energy sets. Compare to exhaustive classical conformer search followed by the same high-level electronic reference and preregistered rank agreement. An independent observer must evaluate independent deduplicated conformer geometries, high-level relative energies and tie-aware Kendall tau calculated on withheld structures. Blinded adversarial intervention: hidden mirror-image stereoisomer and duplicate-conformer injection before blinded re-ranking. Potentially stronger rival: undersampled conformers, duplicate conformer labels or biased tie treatment falsely improving agreement. Hard stop: unresolved stereoisomer identity, insufficient conformer coverage, unstable ranking under resampling or ill-defined Kendall tau denominator. This is a research-design contract, not a newly verified gain. Successor interpretation: model, molecular identity, reference and reported uncertainty travel together. No favorable synthetic numerical residual should be substituted for a molecule-specific converged quantum calculation. In F122, the strongest classical analysis may win. Preserve all unsuccessful inputs, problematic spin or photochemical states and withheld counterexamples. A research gate is an invitation to reject the model when evidence requires it. F123 / Quantum-Chemical Models of Aroma–Olfactory-Receptor Binding at the Limit The proposed physical object is molecular interaction energy of odorant ligands and uncertain receptor-pocket models, with emphasis on ligand protonation, flexible receptor pocket geometry, solvent dielectric screening, dispersion interactions, desolvation, entropy, charge assignment and uncertain structural identity. Primary decision: Receptor-binding energy prediction MAE [kJ/mol]. The minimum reproducible prototype needs documented synthetic ligand-pocket cluster coordinates, archived reference structures and separately labelled hypothetical receptor conformations. Compare to matched classical force-field plus high-level cluster quantum chemistry with explicit solvation controls and an independent binding reference if available. An independent observer must evaluate holdout geometry and binding-energy benchmark with independent structural annotation and environmental assumptions. Blinded adversarial intervention: blind receptor-pocket rotamer and protonation swap with a decoy ligand of identical size. Potentially stronger rival: docking pose selection or solvent/protonation mismatch yielding attractive computed energies without genuine binding. Hard stop: undefined receptor structure or protonation, no legitimate reference binding energy, uncorrected double-counting or model interpreting binding as sensory effect. This is a research-design contract, not a newly verified gain. Successor interpretation: model, molecular identity, reference and reported uncertainty travel together. No favorable synthetic numerical residual should be substituted for a molecule-specific converged quantum calculation. In F123, the strongest classical analysis may win. Preserve all unsuccessful inputs, problematic spin or photochemical states and withheld counterexamples. A research gate is an invitation to reject the model when evidence requires it. F124 / Quantum Chemistry of Essential-Oil Oxidation Pathways at the Limit The proposed physical object is oxidative transition states and competing reaction pathways for terpene constituents, with emphasis on radical initiation, oxygen addition, hydrogen transfer, conformer-dependent transition states, spin-state crossings, intrinsic reaction coordinates, zero-point corrections and branching competing channels. Primary decision: Oxidation transition-state energy error [kJ/mol]. The minimum reproducible prototype needs digitally defined terpene oxidation reactants, radicals and transition-state coordinate sets; no synthesized reactive intermediates. Compare to same-stationary-point reference transition-state energies using established electronic-structure methods with vibrational and IRC verification. An independent observer must evaluate independent harmonic frequency/IRC files, matched reaction states, oxygen accounting and high-level reference barrier energies. Blinded adversarial intervention: withheld spin-state and competing oxygen-addition channel with randomized path labels. Potentially stronger rival: wrong saddle order, missing radical branch, inconsistent spin reference or mismatched zero-point energy. Hard stop: transition structure without one valid imaginary mode and connected IRC, unaccounted oxygen stoichiometry or severe reference-state mismatch. This is a research-design contract, not a newly verified gain. Successor interpretation: model, molecular identity, reference and reported uncertainty travel together. No favorable synthetic numerical residual should be substituted for a molecule-specific converged quantum calculation. In F124, the strongest classical analysis may win. Preserve all unsuccessful inputs, problematic spin or photochemical states and withheld counterexamples. A research gate is an invitation to reject the model when evidence requires it. F125 / Photochemical Degradation of Aroma Molecules at the Limit The proposed physical object is light-driven transformation rates, absorption cross sections and competing oxygen pathways, with emphasis on wavelength-dependent photon absorption, excited-state quantum yield, oxygen-quenching, radical photoproduct branches, nonradiative loss and dark-reaction baselines. Primary decision: Photochemical degradation rate coefficient [h^-1]. The minimum reproducible prototype needs traceable simulated terpene chromophores, documented absorption spectra and synthetic photon flux distributions with reference lamp metadata. Compare to classical spectral photokinetic model with measured lamp spectrum, blanks and matched dark control; high-level photochemical calculations for candidate cross-sections. An independent observer must evaluate independent actinometry, spectrum-resolved photolysis and chemical parent/product inventory from a future experiment. Blinded adversarial intervention: concealed wavelength filter swap, oxygen-clamp reversal and dark-control code exchange. Potentially stronger rival: spectral lamp drift, oxygen ingress or parent-molecule assay loss masquerading as photolytic degradation. Hard stop: unmeasured lamp spectrum, missing parent-plus-photoproduct balance, nonidentified reaction rate or unstable photon-dose calibration. Units: E_calc and E_ref in Hartree; 2625.4996 kJ/mol per Hartree; Delta_E kJ/mol. 3D: A reference-residual valley across basis size and conformer count. F121 / Absolute electronic-energy error: MAE = sum(abs(E_i-E_ref,i))/N. Units: All energies kJ/mol; N distinct held-out molecules; MAE kJ/mol. 3D: An error basin whose apparently low corner may omit difficult structures. F121 / Variational state energy: E_var = <psi|H|psi>/<psi|psi>. Units: Numerator energy in Hartree and denominator dimensionless; E_var Hartree. 3D: A variational saddle reflects ansatz expressivity, not quantum advantage. F121 / Basis-set extrapolation: E(X) = E_inf + A*X^(-3). Units: E and A Hartree; cardinal X dimensionless; single-reference asymptotic assumption. 3D: A convergence ridge flattening as X rises. F121 / Molecular energy error uncertainty: u_diff = sqrt(u_calc^2+u_ref^2-2*cov). Units: Both uncertainties Hartree; covariance Hartree^2; u_diff Hartree. 3D: An uncertainty contour may hide correlated reference errors. F121 / Energy improvement per compute cost: G = (MAE_ref-MAE_new)/Cost. Units: Numerator kJ/mol; cost CPU-hour/molecule; G kJ*mol^-1/(CPU-hour/molecule). 3D: The gain-cost ridge may reverse under a full compute budget. F122 / Periodic torsion potential: V(phi)=V0+sum[V_n*(1+cos(n*phi-delta_n))/2]. Units: V0,Vn kJ/mol; phi and phase in radians inside cosine; V kJ/mol. 3D: Periodic torsional ridges identify alternate basins. F122 / Boltzmann conformer probability: p_i=exp(-DeltaE_i/(R*T))/Z. Units: DeltaE kJ/mol; R=0.008314 kJ/(mol*K); T K; Z dimensionless. 3D: Temperature-dependent basin population envelope. F122 / Tie-corrected Kendall agreement: tau_b=(C-D)/sqrt((C+D+Tx)*(C+D+Ty)). Units: C,D,Tx,Ty counts; tau dimensionless in [-1,1]. 3D: Rank-agreement saddle differs from minimum-energy error surface. F122 / Conformer energy root mean square: RMSE=sqrt(sum((Ei-Erefi)^2)/N). Units: E and reference in kJ/mol; result kJ/mol. 3D: An RMSE crest detects catastrophic outliers hidden by rank scores. F122 / Relative partition free energy: F=-R*T*ln(sum_i exp(-DeltaEi/(R*T))). Units: R kJ/(mol*K); T K; F kJ/mol relative to stated energy zero. 3D: A population valley varies with conformer entropy. F122 / Conformer effective sample number: Neff=1/sum_i(p_i^2). Units: p_i dimensionless and normalized; Neff effective count. 3D: Sparse-count plateau indicates a misleading landscape. F123 / Cluster binding energy difference: DeltaE_bind=E_complex-E_receptor-E_ligand. Units: All E in kJ/mol and same electronic reference, charge and basis; DeltaE kJ/mol. 3D: A binding-energy well sensitive to solvent and pose. F123 / Pocket interaction energy error: MAE_bind=sum(abs(Gpred-Gref))/N. Units: All G kJ/mol in the same thermodynamic reference convention. 3D: A hidden pose change can create a false error minimum. F123 / Screened electrostatic interaction: E_C=(NA/(1000*4*pi*eps0*epsr))*sum(qi*qj/rij). Units: qi C, r m, eps0 F/m, NA mol^-1; result kJ/mol. 3D: A dielectric dependent Coulomb valley. F123 / Conformational ensemble binding free energy: DeltaG_eff=-R*T*ln(sum_i p_i*exp(-DeltaG_i/(R*T))). Units: R kJ/(mol*K), T K, G kJ/mol; p_i normalized. 3D: A multi-pocket basin changes under ensemble reweighting. F123 / Binding entropy correction: DeltaG=DeltaH-T*DeltaS. Units: DeltaH kJ/mol; DeltaS kJ/(mol*K); T K; DeltaG kJ/mol. 3D: Entropy term produces a temperature-dependent saddle. F123 / Binding prediction normalized error: z=(G_pred-G_ref)/u_G. Units: G and uncertainty u_G kJ/mol; z dimensionless. 3D: A standardized residual frontier diagnoses false confidence. F124 / Oxidation activation barrier: DeltaE_dagger=E_TS-E_reactants. Units: E_TS and E_reactants kJ/mol with same charge/spin and ZPE convention. 3D: A reaction coordinate saddle must be independently verified. F124 / Transition barrier prediction error: epsilon_TS=DeltaE_dagger,pred-DeltaE_dagger,ref. Units: Both barriers kJ/mol in matching reference convention; error kJ/mol. 3D: A basis-dependent error valley can hide missing reaction channels. F124 / Eyring transition state rate: k=(kB*T/h)*exp(-DeltaG_dagger/(R*T)). Units: kB*T/h s^-1; DeltaG_dagger and RT J/mol; k s^-1. 3D: Rate curvature amplifies modest barrier differences. F124 / Activation free-energy identity: DeltaG_dagger=DeltaH_dagger-T*DeltaS_dagger. Units: DeltaH J/mol; DeltaS J/(mol*K); T K; result J/mol. 3D: Entropy-driven crossing shows why electronic barrier is not Gibbs barrier. F124 / Reaction branching fraction: f_i=k_i/sum_j(k_j). Units: All competing rate constants in same time unit; f dimensionless. 3D: Competing channels make ridges instead of a single preferred path. F124 / Vibrational saddle requirement: N_imag(TS)=1. Units: Count of imaginary harmonic frequencies; dimensionless integer. 3D: A discrete topology gate, not a smooth empirical surface. F125 / Apparent first-order photolysis rate: k_app=-d[ln(C/C0)]/dt. Units: C and C0 same units; t h; k_app h^-1, only within first-order regime. 3D: Decay-rate ridge must match independent parent/product inventory. F125 / Photon-flux photolysis kernel: k_photo=3600*integral(phi(lam)*sigma(lam)*F(lam)dlam). Units: Quantum yield phi dimensionless; sigma m2; spectral photon flux integrated photons/(m2*s); k h^-1. 3D: Action-spectrum crest follows wavelength-resolved absorption. F125 / Beer-Lambert optical absorbance: A=epsilon*c*l. Units: epsilon L/(mol*cm), c mol/L, l cm; absorbance dimensionless. 3D: Absorbance saturation ridge violates linear small-signal expectation. F125 / Molecular photolysis quantum yield: phi=N_reacted/N_absorbed. Units: Photon and reacted molecule counts; phi dimensionless in simple one-photon pathway. 3D: Yield valley tests competing relaxation channels. F125 / Integrated photon fluence: H_photon=integral(F_photon(t) dt). Units: F photons/(m2*s); dt s; fluence photons/m2. 3D: Fluence contours expose different intensity-time schedules. F125 / Photo-dark competing reaction rates: k_total=k_photo+k_dark+k_oxygen. Units: All k in h^-1 for same parent species and valid first-order approximation. 3D: Oxygen-pressure saddle distinguishes independent reaction paths. The sixth preserves failed input decks and a binding stopping rule. summary: This archive contains the occurrence datasets, environmental predictor sets, projected habitat-suitability rasters, derived tables and analysis code supporting the study "Climate-driven shifts in the potential distributions and spatial overlap of pear (Pyrus spp.) and the oriental fruit moth (Grapholita molesta) in China" (Geng et al.). Contents 01_occurrences/ - Spatially filtered occurrence records used for modelling: Pyrus_spp_occurrences.csv (n = 1063) and G_molesta_occurrences.csv (n = 108), with fields record_id, taxon, longitude, latitude, source (GBIF / iNaturalist / literature) and year. Derived from 2327 Pyrus and 139 G. molesta raw records by removing duplicates and applying 5 x 5 km spatial filtering in ENMTools. 02_environmental_variables/ - The 40 candidate variables (19 bioclimatic, 3 topographic, 18 soil) with their provenance, the sets retained after Pearson (|r| < 0.8) and VIF (< 5) screening, and the final predictor sets at 2.5 arc-min: Pyrus spp. = Bio2, Bio4, Bio6, Elevation, Aspect, Slope, T-CaCO3, T-CaSO4; G. molesta = Bio1, Bio4, Bio19, Elevation, Aspect, Slope, T-CaCO3, T-pH-H2O. 03_kuenm_optimisation/ - kuenm calibration output: 600 candidate parameter sets (regularization multiplier 0.1-4.0 crossed with 15 feature-class combinations) ranked by delta AICc. Selected settings: RM = 0.8, FC = LPT for Pyrus spp.; RM = 3.7, FC = QT for G. molesta. 04_suitability_rasters/ - Projected habitat suitability (GeoTIFF, 2.5 arc-min, China extent) for the current baseline (1970-2000, WorldClim) and the 2050s, 2070s and 2090s under SSP126, SSP245 and SSP585 (BCC-CSM2-MR), for both taxa, from the optimised MaxEnt models and the Biomod2 committee-averaging (EMca) ensembles, together with the species-level MaxEnt models for P. pyrifolia, P. ussuriensis and P. bretschneideri. 05_area_overlap/ - Suitable area by suitability class (threshold >= 0.2), change rates relative to current, spatial overlap extent, Jaccard indices among species-level models, and centroid displacements for each period and scenario. 06_scripts/ - R and shell scripts for MaxEnt and kuenm calibration, Biomod2 ensemble modelling (10 algorithms, 10 replicates, pseudo-absence to presence ratio 10:1 with a 5 km minimum distance), MESS extrapolation diagnostics, thresholding, area and centroid calculation and overlap analysis. Run order and required package versions are given in README.txt. 07_tables/ - Manuscript Tables 4-7 as csv: variable percent contribution and permutation importance, projected suitable areas and species-level model performance. Methods summary MaxEnt 3.4.4 was run with kuenm-optimised settings; ensemble models were built in Biomod2 with the six top-performing algorithms and integrated by committee averaging; calibration and evaluation followed a 75/25 split, and performance was assessed with AUC, TSS and Kappa. All layers were standardized to 2.5 arc-min. Notes The Pyrus occurrence set comprises genus-level records rather than verified commercial orchard locations, so the projections represent climatic suitability for the sampled Pyrus occurrences and not cultivated pear production area. Raw records originate from GBIF (https://www.gbif.org) and iNaturalist (https://www.inaturalist.org) and remain under their original licences; this archive provides the filtered, modelling-ready derivatives. Author contributions are given in the additional description. Contact: gengqf@sdau.edu.cn
title: Data and code for: Climate-driven shifts in the potential distributions and spatial overlap of pear (Pyrus spp.) and the oriental fruit moth (Grapholita molesta) in China

summary: Overview This versioned reproducibility archive supports the manuscript Earthquake Waiting Times Adjusted for Seismicity Rate: Implications for Short-Term Forecasting . The study evaluates whether adjusting earthquake waiting times for the seismicity rate estimated by an epidemic-type aftershock sequence (ETAS) model can improve short-term earthquake forecasts. The proposed model (M2) is compared with temporal ETAS (N0), a constant-weight two-component model (M1), and a model using ordinary waiting times with a fixed reference rate (D1). Synthetic experiments also consider a magnitude-weighted alternative (N1). What's New in Version 1.1 Version 1.1 preserves the original version 1.0 archive and adds: Available protocols and results from additional historical earthquake sequences, including exploratory Cohort B and the 18-sequence geographically stratified Cohort C. Event catalogs, forecast scores, model-fitting outputs, and diagnostic analyses. Profile-likelihood investigations of practical parameter identifiability. Parameter-boundary sensitivity experiments involving the Omori decay exponent and exponential triggering timescale. Detailed analyses of the 2011 Tohoku, 2012 Haida Gwaii, and 2017 Iran–Iraq earthquake sequences. Reproducibility documentation, provenance records, and SHA-256 integrity checks. Main Scientific Findings Forecast performance varies across earthquake sequences. Although rate-adjusted waiting times improve retrospective forecast scores in some cases, the results do not demonstrate consistent superiority over ETAS or matched ordinary-waiting-time alternatives. Some apparent improvements depend on the fitted model parameters and their allowable bounds. Nearly equivalent calibration fits can produce substantially different forecasts, including reversals in model ranking. Scope and Limitations The additional global evaluations are retrospective hindcasts, not independently issued prospective forecasts. The available Cohort A component contains the study protocol but not complete final scored results. The Vanuatu audit addendum does not establish verified prospective forecast skill. The parameter-sensitivity analyses are diagnostic and do not establish structural parameter identifiability. Reproducibility The archive contains source code, available input catalogs, fitting outputs, forecast scores, documentation, and checksum manifests. Users should consult README_START_HERE.md , RELEASE_NOTES_v1.1.md , and CLAIM_TO_ARCHIVE_MAP.csv before reproducing individual experiments. The original version 1.0 archive is preserved unchanged within the version 1.1 package.
title: Earthquake Waiting Times Adjusted for Seismicity Rate: Reproducibility Data, Code, and Forecast Evaluation

summary: Data and code for the article Jurisdiction Compliance Gaps Beyond Korea: Transferring Regulatory RAG for Process Plant Engineering to Five Other Jurisdictions (Yuyong Kim). The article reruns the three published case studies of Kim (2026, J. Loss Prev. Process Ind. 103, 106100) with only the jurisdiction changed, over 425,815 indexed provisions of Korea, the US, the EU, Japan, India and China, and evaluates a 70-case US OSHA/EPA benchmark (369,876 documents) with full-text, dense, hybrid and reranked retrieval, a section-hint ablation and gap-classification baselines. The archive contains the benchmark, the obligation anchor map with the accepted alternatives and the corrected gap labels, the stored outputs behind every number reported in the article, the scripts and source modules that produce them, and the figure files. Search indexes and vectors are not included: the eCFR index is rebuilt from the public eCFR API with the commands in README.md, the other jurisdiction indexes are built by the repository's harvest packs, and the KOSHA documents are not redistributed. Data are released under CC BY 4.0 and code under the GNU Affero General Public License v3.0 (LICENSE_code.txt). Version 2.0.1 corrects the provision-matching rule of the six-jurisdiction case studies (a gold article no longer matches articles whose number merely begins with it, e.g. Article 1 vs Article 13; this changes the EU and China rows) and adds a blind second coding of the answer key. Version 2.0.0 added the case studies, the extended retrieval configurations and the label audit.

summary: What does it mean to say that looking at an atom changes it? A detector can register the same initial average light signal for two proposed measurement processes, even when the processes disturb a trapped ion in different ways. This preprint asks whether a second measurement of the ion’s motion can tell them apart. In a protected three-level calcium-ion benchmark, moving the beam inward at equal calibrated optical gain reduces the initial two-quantum excitation rate by 7.09% under a least-energy-exchange rule and increases it by 23.47% under an energy-frame rule. A scalar optical channel gives zero direct excitation at the inner position. A separate test allows the ion to leave the three levels. Twelve equally sampled preparations give a pooled return probability of exactly one half for original positive rank-one detector events ending within the measured levels. The calibrated scalar model gives 0.999082 at the outer position. Both tests await a matched physical experiment. Published Maryland and Innsbruck apparatus parameters delimit the necessary optical calibration and motional readout. A successful blinded replication would establish which specified rule predicts the disturbance across settings on that instrument. Ordinary quantum measurement theory accommodates the alternatives. The ERU kernel supplies no positive event rate with the probe switched off. This preprint extends An Operator Formulation of the Equation of Relational Unity (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24382197). The deposit includes the experimental protocols, editable manuscript source and reproducibility files.
title: ERU and Wavefunction Collapse: Relational Dynamics, Definite Outcomes and Falsifiable Predictions

summary: Data, fitted models, forecasts and reproducibility code accompanying “Consistency Distillation with Soft Feasibility Penalties and Copula Coupling for Joint Wind-Solar-Load Probabilistic Forecasting”. The archive contains Belgian wind, solar and load hindcasts at 1 h and 24 h, strong tree baselines, retained neural weights and ensembles, calibration and joint-dependence diagnostics, figure source data and table-generation code. Separate experiments examine archived-weather wind forecasts under matched training budgets and complete inference costs for fixed core policies. The weather-budget experiment and inference-cost benchmark use different models and must not be combined into one accuracy–latency claim. The eight ZIP files together form a self-contained archive. Download all parts and extract them into the same directory; each is an ordinary ZIP, not a split volume. ARCHIVE_PARTS.md lists the required files. README.md and REPRODUCE.md describe the directory structure and reproduction commands; MANIFEST.json provides per-file SHA-256 values. Results include negative findings and do not establish qualified-teacher accuracy retention or operational superiority. Author-owned code: MIT. Original experimental results: CC BY 4.0. summary: We establish a deterministic algorithm that computes the exact closed meandric number M_n from the order n in 2^{O(sqrt(n) log n)} bit operations. The main construction splits each crossing into two points and gives a bijection between closed plane meanders and a prescribed class of straight-line Hamilton cycles on a rational point set of size 4n. A polynomial-size system of local annotations selects exactly one constrained Delaunay triangulation for each cycle. Applying the annotated-triangulation counting theorem of Marx and Miltzow then yields the subexponential bound. We make the geometric construction, the uniqueness of every annotation and the integer-arithmetic cost explicit. A technical appendix gives a periodic-depth realization with canonical rooted-path states and the same asymptotic bound. As a separate consequence, an interval decomposition and formal Lagrange inversion give an exact coefficient formula and a subexponential algorithm for an associated core count; these cores are exponentially rare among all meanders. Reproducible finite checks are reported separately from the proof and from larger reference counts. Version 2.0 (22 November 2026): revised and simplified proof of the main reduction, with an explicit c*N^15 bound for the essential annotation catalogue; clearer attribution to the general Marx--Miltzow counting framework; the depth-augmented realization moved to a technical appendix; removal of the former core-coverage theorem section; expanded bibliography and precise reference-count provenance; and reproducible positive, negative and rank-feasibility diagnostics. The accompanying source archive contains editable LaTeX, BibTeX, vector figures, standard-library Python checks and raw records. It does not implement or benchmark the full subexponential counting engine at large orders. This is a preprint and has not been peer reviewed.
title: Exact Subexponential Counting of Closed Plane Meanders

summary: Reproducible by Seed? Not on GPUs: Batch-Dependent Non-Determinism in Text-to-Image Models Text-to-image models are often assumed to be reproducible when the prompt and the random seed are fixed. The paper shows that this does not hold on GPUs. The same prompt and seed can produce a different image when the request is processed inside a batch instead of alone (batch size 1), and the result also changes across GPU models. Replaying exactly the same call is bit-exact, so the differences come from the execution setting (batch shape, numerical precision, GPU) and not from random sampling. This record provides every image used in the image-level analysis of the paper: 3,536 PNG images from 5 models (Qwen-Image-2.1, FLUX 3 Klein, HiDream-O1, Emu3.5 and Janus-Pro-7B), organized into 10 runs. For each prompt: solo images (batch 1, generated twice), batched images and verbatim replays. A static web viewer that shows these images side by side. For each image it tells you whether it is bit-identical to the batch-1 reference and, if not, gives its pixel MAE. Contents t2i_viewer.zip (~73 MB): the viewer, with a small sample (prompts 0, 4 and 8 of every run, 224 images). dataset_test.zip (~1 GB): the full dataset: all 3,536 images, run metadata ( run.json per run), the viewer data file ( manifest.js ) and the original provenance records ( _source/ ). How to view the images No installation is needed, only a web browser. Unzip t2i_viewer.zip and open t2i_viewer/index.html . It shows the sample. To see all the images, unzip dataset_test.zip , copy the resulting dataset_test folder inside t2i_viewer/ (replacing the sample) and reload index.html . The viewer lets you choose a run (model + GPU), a cross-GPU comparison (Janus-Pro-7B on RTX 6000 Ada vs RTX A6000) and, for Janus-Pro-7B, the decoding mode. The amplified difference map in the comparison view needs the folder to be served over HTTP (e.g. python3 -m http.server 8000 inside t2i_viewer/ ). Runs Ten runs, all in bf16: Qwen-Image-2.1 (RTX 6000 Ada, 10 and 100 prompts), FLUX 3 Klein (RTX 6000 Ada, 10 and 100 prompts), HiDream-O1 (RTX 6000 Ada, 100 prompts), Emu3.5 (H100 NVL, 10 prompts) and Janus-Pro-7B (RTX 6000 Ada and RTX A6000, 10 and 100 prompts each). Prompt ids are shared across models. File names (arms) A0.png : solo generation, batch size 1 (the reference). A1.png : solo rerun with the same configuration (bit-identical to A0 in all runs). B_<tag>.png : the same prompt and seed generated inside a batch (e.g. b16-r00-s11 = batch size 16, round 0, slot 11). R_<tag>.png , C_<tag>.png : verbatim replay of a batched call (bit-identical to its batched image in all runs). Janus-Pro-7B file names have a decoding-mode prefix ( sampled- or greedy- ), each with its own A0 reference. Metrics Computed on decoded RGB pixels. Exact means bit-identical RGB data. MAE is the mean absolute pixel difference (0–255 scale) against the A0 of the same prompt and decoding mode. The values are stored in manifest.js and reproduce the paper. Provenance The images were collected from the experiment servers into two dumps ( T2I_v12_images_full_janus_20261121 and T2I_v12_images_full_nonjanus_20261121_b ) and renamed into this layout without modifying their content. The original manifests (with SHA-256 for every image; all 3,536 images match), the collection journal and contact sheets are kept in dataset_test/_source/ . The SDXL images and the fp8/int8 variants discussed in the paper are not included. The images were generated with third-party models; the terms of use of each model may also apply to its outputs.
title: Batch-Dependent Non-Determinism in Text-to-Image Models: Images and Viewer

summary: NovaFabric is self-hosted, open-source replay and evidence infrastructure for AI agents and agentic systems. It captures agent executions as portable, secret-scanned Run Capsules and provides replay, behavioral and structural diff, lineage, cryptographic provenance, assurance, and audit around those executions. The same capture layer can wrap general commands and runs entirely in the user's own infrastructure, from local environments through Kubernetes to SLURM/HPC, with no accounts and no telemetry. It is built around five primitives — Asset Registry, Run Capsule, Replay, Lineage, and Evidence Bundle — and five explicit replay modes (forensic, mocked, semantic, exact, and the experimental intervention mode). Run Capsules can be sealed with the user’s own key; sealing is opt-in. Evidence bundles verify offline using only sha256sum and an ed25519 verifier, with no NovaFabric installation required. Interoperates with established specifications rather than inventing formats: OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions, in-toto/DSSE, RFC 3161 timestamping, W3C PROV, OpenLineage, and CycloneDX.
title: NovaFabric: replayable, verifiable execution evidence for AI agents

summary: A pre-registrable experimental protocol for testing whether the apparent "self" of an LLM agent behaves as a localised, persistent substrate ( ātman ), as a process assembled from the five aggregates with no fixed substrate ( anattā ), or as a surface regularity with no internal organisation (null). It specifies four studies: (1) localisation probes, with targeted, mean and random feature ablation and capability controls; (2) framing invariance of self-descriptions across system personas, languages, registers and role-play framings; (3) aggregate-wise decomposition of activations (rūpa, vedanā, saññā, saṅkhāra, viññāṇa); and (4) impermanence and re-composition across sessions with external memory. It treats self-reports as evidence only when activation-level probes agree with them, and controls for instruction-following, e.g. a model that says "I have no self" after a Buddhist prompt. Provenance. The author wrote this protocol by June 2026 and kept it private in his Notion workspace, attached to the lab page "2026-06-10 – Wadduwage lab summer work plan" under the "citta transformer" project. The file deposited here is byte-for-byte that Notion attachment. Notion's file storage (Amazon S3) reports for it: Last-Modified: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 11:27:24 GMT; MD5 ba4788e1083fa054d4bb670e182ae100; SHA-256 ed1702f18fc5b345d9222ce4ead68ea2415c7e3b3280c522ba8ef0084936a133; 10,389 bytes. It is made public for the first time in this record, on 22 November 2026, and the record's publication date is the date of deposit. Related work by the author. anatta-eval: prompt-level no-self interventions, results and manuscript (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.24444245 ). AI assistance. This protocol was drafted with the help of large language model (LLM) tools under the author's direction. The author set the research question, reviewed the text and takes full responsibility for the content.
title: Testing Anattā in an LLM Agent: A Pre-Registrable Experimental Protocol

summary: Software overview SMART-TDAH is an educational web platform for visualising and analysing students’ exercise results and progress. It combines a React frontend, a Node.js/Express backend and a PostgreSQL connection. It provides user management, progress charts and tables, four interface languages (Galician, Spanish, English and Brazilian Portuguese), and optional language-model-assisted queries through Gemini, LLaMA and Mixtral integrations. Package contents This deposit archives commit 388620adbd23d7793e3af7fec98c6e46a3fea5eb of the Chair’s repository. The package contains 58 original source and resource files, including frontend, backend, dependency manifests and lockfiles, README and GNU GPLv3 licence. A provenance note and file manifest are added. No student database, database dump, API keys or environment credential file is included. Requirements and usage The README documents Node.js 18 or later, npm 9 or later and PostgreSQL 14 or later. Install dependencies separately in the backend and frontend directories. Configure PostgreSQL and API credentials through a local backend .env file. Start the backend with node server.js from its directory and the frontend with npm start . The backend package has no npm start script in this archived version. Database provisioning and credentials must be supplied by the deploying institution. Access and licence The source is openly downloadable under GNU GPL version 3. Preserve the original copyright and licence notices and consult LICENSE . Dependencies and external API services retain their respective terms. Academic context and contributions The software was developed by Ángel Álvarez Rey in a service-learning bachelor’s thesis at Universidade da Coruña, supervised by José Joaquim de Moura Ramos, Jorge Novo Buján and Marcos Ortega Hortas, within the NTT DATA Diversity Chair’s solidarity thesis programme. The project involved educational collaboration with Floriano and Barão de Grajaú, Brazil. Institutional thesis record . Preservation and reuse A version-specific source archive with a persistent identifier, dependency information and deployment documentation supports transparent inspection, reproducibility and adaptation by educational and research institutions. The deposit describes a technical and educational result; it does not establish diagnostic validity, clinical certification or independently quantified adoption. Source and citation Chair’s repository ; student’s repository . Please cite this software version and the associated thesis when using the work in research.
title: SMART-TDAH: Open-Source Web Platform for Educational Progress Analysis and AI-Assisted Queries

summary: This record holds the public collections read by the EARC analysis notebook (earc_analysis.ipynb, software record 10.5281/zenodo.23324439), which audits whether a machine learning score depends on units shared between training and test sets. It contains 101 tables from R packages as distributed by Rdatasets, ten molecular benchmark tables from the chemprop v1.7.1 data archive (MoleculeNet), the ApisTox honey bee toxicity data with its splits, three materials tables, the protein GB1 variants of FLIP, the California housing survey and a monthly excerpt of the Mauna Loa carbon dioxide record. Use: unzip earc-data.zip and attach the folder as an input of the notebook, or set the environment variable EARC_DATA to its path. Retinal images and smartphone activity data are not included; the notebook reads them from their own sources. Licences: every file keeps the licence of its source and is redistributed unchanged, except the Mauna Loa file, an excerpt of a U.S. government record. MANIFEST.csv gives the source address, licence, licence text, citation and DOI of each file; the licence texts and copyright notices required by the sources are in LICENSES/ inside earc-data.zip. ApisTox (CC BY-NC 4.0) and SIDER (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0) may be used for non-commercial purposes only; SIDER and Lipophilicity (CC BY-SA 3.0) adaptations must keep the same licence. Files produced by the author of this record are released under CC BY 4.0. Citation: cite this record (all versions: 10.5281/zenodo.24443560) and the original source of every collection you use, as listed in CITATIONS.md with their DOIs.
title: EARC data bundle: public tabular, molecular, materials and protein collections with sources, licences and citations

summary: STARLI · WHITE RAINBOW ERA · FAMILY 27 · F131-F135 GENERATIVE COMPUTATIONAL DESIGN OF AROMA MOLECULES RESEARCH ESSENCE · PROSPECTIVE / NONCLINICAL / FALSIFIABLE / REPRODUCIBLE FAMILY RESEARCH CONTRACT This family studies five complementary but scientifically distinct aspects of computational design for plant-derived odorants. The central claim is not that a machine can create a beneficial scent. It is a prospectively falsifiable proposal that molecular graph candidates, predicted odour descriptors, volatility-constrained Pareto sets, oxidation-stability models and abstract synthesis-route plausibility can be compared fairly against competent classical baselines. Each flagship uses its own denominator, measurement unit, external witness, negative-case ledger and stopping authority. Computational syntax does not establish real molecular identity; a predicted odour attribute does not verify a human perception; a feasible Pareto set is not a safety certificate; a stable simulation is not an aging experiment; and a synthetic route diagram is not a synthesized compound. The response surfaces throughout the 819-page PDF are synthetic 25-by-25 numerical illustrations intended to illuminate hypothetical shape, sensitivity and non-identifiability. They are not model outputs obtained from new molecular-generation runs. Future groups should preregister sample inclusion, chemical identity, strong nulls, risk exclusions and uncertainty before examining results. Classical models should be allowed to win. FLAGSHIP F131 · Generative Design of Candidate Aroma Molecular Structures at the Limit Scientific object: chemical-graph generation under valence, stereochemistry, scaffold holdout and provenance constraints. Physical basis: SMILES parsing, valence and aromaticity sanitization, canonical graph uniqueness, stereoisomer assignment, charge conservation and training scaffold leakage. Primary endpoint: Chemical validity of generated molecules [%]. Comparator: expert-curated terpene analogues, fragment recombination and a tuned classical SMILES generator at the same proposal budget. Strong rival: memorized scaffolds, duplicate canonical graphs, invalid stereochemistry, biased molecular-size filtering or generator reward hacking. Withheld intervention: sealed scaffold-family holdout with stereochemical and charge-state swaps. Independent observation: independent canonicalization and chemistry-rule audit plus blinded scaffold-novelty registry. Binding stop: unknown graph source, invalid atom valence, missing generator denominator, undisclosed training overlap or unreviewed hazardous candidate. This evidence contract does not transfer its interpretation to unrelated flagships or human therapeutic claims. FLAGSHIP F132 · Bias in Predicting Molecular Odour Properties at the Limit Scientific object: blind structure-to-odour attribute prediction with bias diagnostics across molecular families. Physical basis: olfactory descriptor ontology, multi-label rater uncertainty, scaffold domain shift, molecular representation and panel expectation leakage. Primary endpoint: Blind odour attribute correlation [1]. Comparator: scaffold-held-out random forest, descriptor-based regression and a pre-registered principal-odour-map baseline. Strong rival: semantic descriptor leakage, inconsistent rating scales, panel bias, aromatic-family imbalance or post-hoc attribute selection. Withheld intervention: concealed descriptor renaming, scaffold exclusion and panel-rater disagreement stress test. Independent observation: ethically obtained independent blinded attribute-rating archive with chemistry identity, interrater statistics and external family splits. Binding stop: no ethically sourced sensory reference, uncorrected label leakage, insufficient external families or unstable denominator variance. This evidence contract does not transfer its interpretation to unrelated flagships or human therapeutic claims. FLAGSHIP F133 ·

summary: STARLI · WHITE RAINBOW ERA · FAMILY 26 / F126-F130 QUANTUM AROMA SIMULATION AND EXPERIMENTAL BENCHMARKS · FIVE THOUSAND WORD RESEARCH ESSENCE Prospective / Nonclinical / Falsifiable / Reproducible / All numerical 3D surfaces are synthetic RESEARCH POSITION This scientific working edition specifies separate tests for nanomaterial adsorption-energy calculations, quantum molecular-simulation benchmarks against strong classical methods, blind botanical-isomer spectral identification, solvent/interface free-energy transfer, and uncertainty calibration against experimental aroma analysis. The five outcomes use incompatible denominators: energy mean absolute error in kilojoules per mole, isomer identification accuracy in percent, and externally observed uncertainty coverage in percent. Surface geometries, molecular identities, gas-phase and condensed-phase reference states, classical compute cost, isomer standards, and prediction interval widths cannot be silently exchanged. The forty-two plotted meshes are deterministic synthetic illustrations rather than actual quantum calculations or experiments. Nothing in these figures establishes a materials improvement, neurological effect, human benefit or special quantum healing property. Research inheritance depends on explicit null comparisons, falsifiers, negative cases, working code and externally held evidence. FIVE INDEPENDENT FLAGSHIP CONTRACTS F126 · Calculation of Aroma Adsorption Energies on Nanomaterials at the Limit Research object: adsorption-energy predictions for traceable botanical volatiles on characterized nanomaterial surfaces. Primary endpoint: Adsorption energy MAE [kJ/mol]. Principal physical uncertainty: surface-site heterogeneity, adsorbate orientation, surface coverage, dispersion, substrate relaxation, basis-set superposition error and solvent competition. Strong classical comparator: matched-geometry periodic DFT or established dispersion-corrected classical reference with independently measured desorption if available. Independent scientific witness: independent adsorption reference table with surface identity, adsorption site, coverage, energy conventions and uncertainty. Concealed adversarial perturbation: blind swap of adsorption-site geometry, surface hydroxylation and reference molecule orientation. A rival interpretation is coverage-dependent aggregation, omitted surface hydroxylation, ghost-basis correction or a shifted adsorption reference rather than true improvement. Stop if unknown surface chemistry, missing adsorption reference state, energy sign inconsistency, uncontrolled basis or incomplete mass accounting. This is a prospective design rather than a verified result. F127 · Quantum-Computing Benchmarks for Aroma Molecular Simulation at the Limit Research object: equal-budget quantum-circuit and classical molecule-simulation benchmarking. Primary endpoint: Equal-resource quantum simulation error [kJ/mol]. Principal physical uncertainty: active-space selection, fermion-to-qubit mapping, variational ansatz expressivity, measurement shots, circuit depth, gate noise, error mitigation and total wall-time cost. Strong classical comparator: strong classical electronic-structure baseline and noiseless quantum simulator at the same molecule and explicit wall-time, energy and precision budget. Independent scientific witness: independent reference energy and auditable device/simulator circuit, shot, calibration, compiler and runtime ledger. Concealed adversarial perturbation: withheld spin/active-space perturbation combined with a noisy-shot and calibration-day reversal. A rival interpretation is reference leakage, noise mitigation bias, inconsistent active space, cherry-picked molecule or ignored overhead. Stop if absence of matched classical resource ledger, unreproducible measurement statistics, unstable optimizer or unreported hardware calibration. This is a prospective design rather than a verified result. F128 · Sp

Each question has a different kind of observable. F121, F123 and F124 require energy-error units in kJ/mol; F122 requires dimensionless Kendall rank agreement; F125 uses h^-1 for a first-order kinetic coefficient. Shared molecular metadata cannot make these numerical quantities interchangeable. Forty-two synthetic three-dimensional meshes visualize possibilities, not results computed for an actual terpene. No new quantum chemistry benchmark was performed on real molecule-specific input decks; no receptor experiment, inhalation study, skin assay or clinical efficacy study was conducted. The proposed methods need independent references, uncertainty accounting, matched computational budgets and preregistered reasons to stop. A high-level classical method may outperform every newer architecture and remains a scientifically useful answer. THE SIX-STAGE CHAPTER DEVELOPMENT In the first passage the investigator identifies physical origin, material identity and the inherited scientific dispute. The second passage proposes a specific physical mechanism and a mathematical geometry with separate units on each axis. The third passage audits calibration, independent measurements and all denominators. The fourth introduces an adversarial counterfactual designed to preserve a plausible visible outcome while changing the cause. The fifth tests the strongest equal-resource comparator, including blinded disturbances and uncertainty intervals. The sixth leaves an open source inheritance with a hard stopping rule and a future research question. The progression must change the question at each step; simply altering the names of variables would not constitute scientific development. TWO HUNDRED RESEARCH GATES The gates follow forty specific challenges for each of five distinct flagship endpoints. Every gate has a material or informational origin, an extreme counterfactual revealing how a false interpretation might survive and a future plan with an independent witness. Each gate includes a concept structure and an adversarial-break structure. Their diagrams explain competing roles; they do not prove that the proposed mechanisms work. The gate remains open when an outside investigator discovers a new, better explanation and can reproduce the experiment without asking the originator for private knowledge. THIRTY-THREE PHOENIX PROTOTYPES Each Phoenix object proposes a physical or digital minimum that could be independently built: a chemical identity card, sensor calibration fixture, adversarial controller, locked sensor model, offline reconstruction package or simulated archive migration. A prototype is an answer embryo, not a certified product. Its design is useful only if it identifies an independent observation that could make the present answer fail, and if the human operator retains the right to stop the test. ONE-HUNDRED-YEAR ARCHIVAL TEST The century-scale horizon is modeled, not observed. It contains threats such as changing formats, missing dependencies, lost institutional custody, inaccessible computing services and silent changes to research methods. The preferred experiment uses adversarial simulated migrations and independent replay across distinct custody pathways. A successor should be able to identify the original chemical evidence, recreate model grids, verify denominators and revoke inherited control privileges. A beautiful future image without these rights is insufficient. FINAL SCIENTIFIC INSCRIPTION The future is not an extension of a beautiful prediction. It is an invitation to test the parts of today's knowledge that might be wrong. The White Rainbow Era seeks a defensible warmth: open knowledge, human authority, bounded instruments, adequate reference comparisons and the inheritance of questions. THE SIX-STAGE CHAPTER DEVELOPMENT In the first passage the investigator identifies physical origin, material identity and the inherited scientific dispute. The second passage proposes a specific physical mechanism and a mathematical geometry with separate units on each axis. The third passage audits calibration, independent measurements and all denominators. The fourth introduces an adversarial counterfactual designed to preserve a plausible visible outcome while changing the cause. The fifth tests the strongest equal-resource comparator, including blinded disturbances and uncertainty intervals. The sixth leaves an open source inheritance with a hard stopping rule and a future research question. The progression must change the question at each step; simply altering the names of variables would not constitute scientific development. TWO HUNDRED RESEARCH GATES The gates follow forty specific challenges for each of five distinct flagship endpoints. Every gate has a material or informational origin, an extreme counterfactual revealing how a false interpretation might survive and a future plan with an independent witness. Each gate includes a concept structure and an adversarial-break structure. Their diagrams explain competing roles; they do not prove that the proposed mechanisms work. The gate remains open when an outside investigator discovers a new, better explanation and can reproduce the experiment without asking the originator for private knowledge. THIRTY-THREE PHOENIX PROTOTYPES Each Phoenix object proposes a physical or digital minimum that could be independently built: a chemical identity card, sensor calibration fixture, adversarial controller, locked sensor model, offline reconstruction package or simulated archive migration. A prototype is an answer embryo, not a certified product. Its design is useful only if it identifies an independent observation that could make the present answer fail, and if the human operator retains the right to stop the test. ONE-HUNDRED-YEAR ARCHIVAL TEST The century-scale horizon is modeled, not observed. It contains threats such as changing formats, missing dependencies, lost institutional custody, inaccessible computing services and silent changes to research methods. The preferred experiment uses adversarial simulated migrations and independent replay across distinct custody pathways. A successor should be able to identify the original chemical evidence, recreate model grids, verify denominators and revoke inherited control privileges. A beautiful future image without these rights is insufficient. FINAL SCIENTIFIC INSCRIPTION The future is not an extension of a beautiful prediction. It is an invitation to test the parts of today's knowledge that might be wrong. The White Rainbow Era seeks a defensible warmth: open knowledge, human authority, bounded instruments, adequate reference comparisons and the inheritance of questions. THE SIX-STAGE CHAPTER DEVELOPMENT In the first passage the investigator identifies physical origin, material identity and the inherited scientific dispute. The second passage proposes a specific physical mechanism and a mathematical geometry with separate units on each axis. The third passage audits calibration, independent measurements and all denominators. The fourth introduces an adversarial counterfactual designed to preserve a plausible visible outcome while changing the cause. The fifth tests the strongest equal-resource comparator, including blinded disturbances and uncertainty intervals. The sixth leaves an open source inheritance with a hard stopping rule and a future research question. The progression must change the question at each step; simply altering the names of variables would not constitute scientific development. TWO HUNDRED RESEARCH GATES The gates follow forty specific challenges for each of five distinct flagship endpoints. Every gate has a material or informational origin, an extreme counterfactual revealing how a false interpretation might survive and a future plan with an independent witness. Each gate includes a concept structure and an adversarial-break structure. Their diagrams explain competing roles; they do not prove that the proposed mechanisms work. The gate remains open when an outside investigator discovers a new, better explanation and can reproduce the experiment without asking the originator for private knowledge. THIRTY-THREE PHOENIX PROTOTYPES Each Phoenix object proposes a physical or digital minimum that could be independently built: a chemical identity card, sensor calibration fixture, adversarial controller, locked sensor model, offline reconstruction package or simulated archive migration. A prototype is an answer embryo, not a certified product. Its design is useful only if it identifies an independent observation that could make the present answer fail, and if the human operator retains the right to stop the test. ONE-HUNDRED-YEAR ARCHIVAL TEST The century-scale horizon is modeled, not observed. It contains threats such as changing formats, missing dependencies, lost institutional custody, inaccessible computing services and silent changes to research methods. The preferred experiment uses adversarial simulated migrations and independent replay across distinct custody pathways. A successor should be able to identify the original chemical evidence, recreate model grids, verify denominators and revoke inherited control privileges. A beautiful future image without these rights is insufficient. FINAL SCIENTIFIC INSCRIPTION The future is not an extension of a beautiful prediction. It is an invitation to test the parts of today's knowledge that might be wrong. The White Rainbow Era seeks a defensible warmth: open knowledge, human authority, bounded instruments, adequate reference comparisons and the inheritance of questions. THE SIX-STAGE CHAPTER DEVELOPMENT In the first passage the investigator identifies physical origin, material identity and the inherited scientific dispute. The second passage proposes a specific physical mechanism and a mathematical geometry with separate units on each axis. The third passage audits calibration, independent measurements and all denominators. The fourth introduces an adversarial counterfactual designed to preserve a plausible visible outcome while changing the cause. The fifth tests the strongest equal-resource comparator, including blinded disturbances and uncertainty intervals. The sixth leaves an open source inheritance with a hard stopping rule and a future research question. The progression must change the question at each step; simply altering the names of variables would not constitute scientific development. TWO HUNDRED RESEARCH GATES The gates follow forty specific challenges for each of five distinct flagship endpoints. Every gate has a material or informational origin, an extreme counterfactual revealing how a false interpretation might survive and a future plan with an independent witness. Each gate includes a concept structure and an adversarial-break structure. Their diagrams explain competing roles; they do not prove that the proposed mechanisms work. The gate remains open when an outside investigator discovers a new, better explanation and can reproduce the experiment without asking the originator for private knowledge. THIRTY-THREE PHOENIX PROTOTYPES Each Phoenix object proposes a physical or digital minimum that could be independently built: a chemical identity card, sensor calibration fixture, adversarial controller, locked sensor model, offline reconstruction package or simulated archive migration. A prototype is an answer embryo, not a certified product. Its design is useful only if it identifies an independent observation that could make the present answer fail, and if the human operator retains the right to stop the test. ONE-HUNDRED-YEAR ARCHIVAL TEST The century-scale horizon is modeled, not observed. It contains threats such as changing formats, missing dependencies, lost institutional custody, inaccessible computing services and silent changes to research methods. The preferred experiment uses adversarial simulated migrations and independent replay across distinct custody pathways. A successor should be able to identify the original chemical evidence, recreate model grids, verify denominators and revoke inherited control privileges. A beautiful future image without these rights is insufficient. FINAL SCIENTIFIC INSCRIPTION The future is not an extension of a beautiful prediction. It is an invitation to test the parts of today's knowledge that might be wrong. The White Rainbow Era seeks a defensible warmth: open knowledge, human authority, bounded instruments, adequate reference comparisons and the inheritance of questions. THE SIX-STAGE CHAPTER DEVELOPMENT In the first passage the investigator identifies physical origin, material identity and the inherited scientific dispute. The second passage proposes a specific physical mechanism and a mathematical geometry with separate units on each axis. The third passage audits calibration, independent measurements and all denominators. The fourth introduces an adversarial counterfactual designed to preserve a plausible visible outcome while changing the cause. The fifth tests the strongest equal-resource comparator, including blinded disturbances and uncertainty intervals. The sixth leaves an open source inheritance with a hard stopping rule and a future research question. The progression must change the question at each step; simply altering the names of variables would not constitute scientific development. TWO HUNDRED RESEARCH GATES The gates follow forty specific challenges for each of five distinct flagship endpoints. Every gate has a material or informational origin, an extreme counterfactual revealing how a false interpretation might survive and a future plan with an independent witness. Each gate includes a concept structure and an adversarial-break structure. Their diagrams explain competing roles; they do not prove that the proposed mechanisms work. The gate remains open when an outside investigator discovers a new, better explanation and can reproduce the experiment without asking the originator for private knowledge. THIRTY-THREE PHOENIX PROTOTYPES Each Phoenix object proposes a physical or digital minimum that could be independently built: a chemical identity card, sensor calibration fixture, adversarial controller, locked sensor model, offline reconstruction package or simulated archive migration. A prototype is an answer embryo, not a certified product. Its design is useful only if it identifies an independent observation that could make the present answer fail, and if the human operator retains the right to stop the test. ONE-HUNDRED-YEAR ARCHIVAL TEST The century-scale horizon is modeled, not observed. It contains threats such as changing formats, missing dependencies, lost institutional custody, inaccessible computing services and silent changes to research methods. The preferred experiment uses adversarial simulated migrations and independent replay across distinct custody pathways. A successor should be able to identify the original chemical evidence, recreate model grids, verify denominators and revoke inherited control privileges. A beautiful future image without these rights is insufficient. FINAL SCIENTIFIC INSCRIPTION The future is not an extension of a beautiful prediction. It is an invitation to test the parts of today's knowledge that might be wrong. The White Rainbow Era seeks a defensible warmth: open knowledge, human authority, bounded instruments, adequate reference comparisons and the inheritance of questions. THE SIX-STAGE CHAPTER DEVELOPMENT In the first passage the investigator identifies physical origin, material identity and the inherited scientific dispute. The second passage proposes a specific physical mechanism and a mathematical geometry with separate units on each axis. The third passage audits calibration, independent measurements and all denominators. The fourth introduces an adversarial counterfactual designed to preserve a plausible visible outcome while changing the cause. The fifth tests the strongest equal-resource comparator, including blinded disturbances and uncertainty intervals. The sixth leaves an open source inheritance with a hard stopping rule and a future research question. The progression must change the question at each step; simply altering the names of variables would not constitute scientific development. TWO HUNDRED RESEARCH GATES The gates follow forty specific challenges for each of five distinct flagship endpoints. Every gate has a material or informational origin, an extreme counterfactual revealing how a false interpretation might survive and a future plan with an independent witness. Each gate includes a concept structure and an adversarial-break structure. Their diagrams explain competing roles; they do not prove that the proposed mechanisms work. The gate remains open when an outside investigator discovers a new, better explanation and can reproduce the experiment without asking the originator for private knowledge. THIRTY-THREE PHOENIX PROTOTYPES Each Phoenix object proposes a physical or digital minimum that could be independently built: a chemical identity card, sensor calibration fixture, adversarial controller, locked sensor model, offline reconstruction package or simulated archive migration. A prototype is an answer embryo, not a certified product. Its design is useful only if it identifies an independent observation that could make the present answer fail, and if the human operator retains the right to stop the test. ONE-HUNDRED-YEAR ARCHIVAL TEST The century-scale horizon is modeled, not observed. It contains threats such as changing formats, missing dependencies, lost institutional custody, inaccessible computing services and silent changes to research methods. The preferred experiment uses adversarial simulated migrations and independent replay across distinct custody pathways. A successor should be able to identify the original chemical evidence, recreate model grids, verify denominators and revoke inherited control privileges. A beautiful future image without these rights is insufficient. FINAL SCIENTIFIC INSCRIPTION The future is not an extension of a beautiful prediction. It is an invitation to test the parts of today's knowledge that might be wrong. The White Rainbow Era seeks a defensible warmth: open knowledge, human authority, bounded instruments, adequate reference comparisons and the inheritance of questions. THE SIX-STAGE CHAPTER DEVELOPMENT In the first passage the investigator identifies physical origin, material identity and the inherited scientific dispute. The second passage proposes a specific physical mechanism and a mathematical geometry with separate units on each axis. The third passage audits calibration, independent measurements and all denominators. The fourth introduces an adversarial counterfactual designed to preserve a plausible visible outcome while changing the cause. The fifth tests the strongest equal-resource comparator, including blinded disturbances and uncertainty intervals. The sixth leaves an open source inheritance with a hard stopping rule and a future research question. The progression must change the question at each step; simply altering the names of variables would not constitute scientific development. TWO HUNDRED RESEARCH GATES The gates follow forty specific challenges for each of five distinct flagship endpoints. Every gate has a material or informational origin, an extreme counterfactual revealing how a false interpretation might survive and a future plan with an independent witness. Each gate includes a concept structure and an adversarial-break structure. Their diagrams explain competing roles; they do not prove that the proposed mechanisms work. The gate remains open when an outside investigator discovers a new, better explanation and can reproduce the experiment without asking the originator for private knowledge. THIRTY-THREE PHOENIX PROTOTYPES Each Phoenix object proposes a physical or digital minimum that could be independently built: a chemical identity card, sensor calibration fixture, adversarial controller, locked sensor model, offline reconstruction package or simulated archive migration. A prototype is an answer embryo, not a certified product. Its design is useful only if it identifies an independent observation that could make the present answer fail, and if the human operator retains the right to stop the test. ONE-HUNDRED-YEAR ARCHIVAL TEST The century-scale horizon is modeled, not observed. It contains threats such as changing formats, missing dependencies, lost institutional custody, inaccessible computing services and silent changes to research methods. The preferred experiment uses adversarial simulated migrations and independent replay across distinct custody pathways. A successor should be able to identify the original chemical evidence, recreate model grids, verify denominators and revoke inherited control privileges. A beautiful future image without these rights is insufficient. FINAL SCIENTIFIC INSCRIPTION The future is not an extension of a beautiful prediction. It is an invitation to test the parts of today's knowledge that might be wrong. The White Rainbow Era seeks a defensible warmth: open knowledge, human authority, bounded instruments, adequate reference comparisons and the inheritance of questions. THE SIX-STAGE CHAPTER DEVELOPMENT In the first passage the investigator identifies physical origin, material identity and the inherited scientific dispute. The second passage proposes a specific physical mechanism and a mathematical geometry with separate units on each axis. The third passage audits calibration, independent measurements and all denominators. The fourth introduces an adversarial counterfactual designed to preserve a plausible visible outcome while changing the cause. The fifth tests the strongest equal-resource comparator, including blinded disturbances and uncertainty intervals. The sixth leaves an open source inheritance with a hard stopping rule and a future research question. The progression must change the question at each step; simply altering the names of variables would not constitute scientific development. TWO HUNDRED RESEARCH GATES The gates follow forty specific challenges for each of five distinct flagship endpoints. Every gate has a material or informational origin, an extreme counterfactual revealing how a false interpretation might survive and a future plan with an independent witness. Each gate includes a concept structure and an adversarial-break structure. Their diagrams explain competing roles; they do not prove that the proposed mechanisms work. The gate remains open when an outside investigator discovers a new, better explanation and can reproduce the experiment without asking the originator for private knowledge. THIRTY-THREE PHOENIX PROTOTYPES Each Phoenix object proposes a physical or digital minimum that could be independently built: a chemical identity card, sensor calibration fixture, adversarial controller, locked sensor model, offline reconstruction package or simulated archive migration. A prototype is an answer embryo, not a certified product. Its design is useful only if it identifies an independent observation that could make the present answer fail, and if the human operator retains the right to stop the test. ONE-HUNDRED-YEAR ARCHIVAL TEST The century-scale horizon is modeled, not observed. It contains threats such as changing formats, missing dependencies, lost institutional custody, inaccessible computing services and silent changes to research methods. The preferred experiment uses adversarial simulated migrations and independent replay across distinct custody pathways. A successor should be able to identify the original chemical evidence, recreate model grids, verify denominators and revoke inherited control privileges. A beautiful future image without these rights is insufficient. FINAL SCIENTIFIC INSCRIPTION The future is not an extension of a beautiful prediction. It is an invitation to test the parts of today's knowledge that might be wrong. The White Rainbow Era seeks a defensible warmth: open knowledge, human authority, bounded instruments, adequate reference comparisons and the inheritance of questions. THE SIX-STAGE CHAPTER DEVELOPMENT In the first passage the investigator identifies physical origin, material identity and the inherited scientific dispute. The second passage proposes a specific physical mechanism and a mathematical geometry with separate units on each axis. The third passage audits calibration, independent measurements and all denominators. The fourth introduces an adversarial counterfactual designed to preserve a plausible visible outcome while changing the cause. The fifth tests the strongest equal-resource comparator, including blinded disturbances and uncertainty intervals. The sixth leaves an open source inheritance with a hard stopping rule and a future research question. The progression must change the question at each step; simply altering the names of variables would not constitute scientific development. TWO HUNDRED RESEARCH GATES The gates follow forty specific challenges for each of five distinct flagship endpoints. Every gate has a material or informational origin, an extreme counterfactual revealing how a false interpretation might survive and a future plan with an independent witness. Each gate includes a concept structure and an adversarial-break structure. Their diagrams explain competing roles; they do not prove that the proposed mechanisms work. The gate remains open when an outside investigator discovers a new, better explanation and can reproduce the experiment without asking the originator for private knowledge. THIRTY-THREE PHOENIX PROTOTYPES Each Phoenix object proposes a physical or digital minimum that could be independently built: a chemical identity card, sensor calibration fixture, adversarial controller, locked sensor model, offline reconstruction package or simulated archive migration. A prototype is an answer embryo, not a certified product. Its design is useful only if it identifies an independent observation that could make the present answer fail, and if the human operator retains the right to stop the test. ONE-HUNDRED-YEAR ARCHIVAL TEST The century-scale horizon is modeled, not observed. It contains threats such as changing formats, missing dependencies, lost institutional custody, inaccessible computing services and silent changes to research methods. The preferred experiment uses adversarial simulated migrations and independent replay across distinct custody pathways. A successor should be able to identify the original chemical evidence, recreate model grids, verify denominators and revoke inherited control privileges. A beautiful future image without these rights is insufficient. FINAL SCIENTIFIC INSCRIPTION The future is not an extension of a beautiful prediction. It is an invitation to test the parts of today's knowledge that might be wrong. The White Rainbow Era seeks a defensible warmth: open knowledge, human authority, bounded instruments, adequate reference comparisons and the inheritance of questions. THE SIX-STAGE CHAPTER DEVELOPMENT In the first passage the investigator identifies physical origin, material identity and the inherited scientific dispute. The second passage proposes a specific physical mechanism and a mathematical geometry with separate units on each axis. The third passage audits calibration, independent measurements and all denominators. The fourth introduces an adversarial counterfactual designed to preserve a plausible visible outcome while changing the cause. The fifth tests the strongest equal-resource comparator, including blinded disturbances and uncertainty intervals. The sixth leaves an open source inheritance with a hard stopping rule and a future research question. The progression must change the question at each step; simply altering the names of variables would not constitute scientific development. TWO HUNDRED RESEARCH GATES The gates follow forty specific challenges for each of five distinct flagship endpoints. Every gate has a material or informational origin, an extreme counterfactual revealing how a false interpretation might survive and a future plan with an independent witness. Each gate includes a concept structure and an adversarial-break structure. Their diagrams explain competing roles; they do not prove that the proposed mechanisms work. The gate remains open when an outside investigator discovers a new, better explanation and can reproduce the experiment without asking the originator for private knowledge. THIRTY-THREE PHOENIX PROTOTYPES Each Phoenix object proposes a physical or digital minimum that could be independently built: a chemical identity card, sensor calibration fixture, adversarial controller, locked sensor model, offline reconstruction package or simulated archive migration. A prototype is an answer embryo, not a certified product. Its design is useful only if it identifies an independent observation that could make the present answer fail, and if the human operator retains the right to stop the test. ONE-HUNDRED-YEAR ARCHIVAL TEST The century-scale horizon is modeled, not observed. It contains threats such as changing formats, missing dependencies, lost institutional custody, inaccessible computing services and silent changes to research methods. The preferred experiment uses adversarial simulated migrations and independent replay across distinct custody pathways. A successor should be able to identify the original chemical evidence, recreate model grids, verify denominators and revoke inherited control privileges. A beautiful future image without these rights is insufficient. FINAL SCIENTIFIC INSCRIPTION The future is not an extension of a beautiful prediction. It is an invitation to test the parts of today's knowledge that might be wrong. The White Rainbow Era seeks a defensible warmth: open knowledge, human authority, bounded instruments, adequate reference comparisons and the inheritance of questions.
