summary: INTEGRATED INTELLIGENT ACUPUNCTURE NANO-QUANTUM RESEARCH AT THE LIMIT F196–F200 · STARLI · White Rainbow Era · Research Working Edition v1.0 Prospective research essence | Nonclinical | Synthetic mathematical models At the end of forty integrated families, the central question changes. How can a research civilization connect five kinds of evidence while preserving the right to disagree? Family 40 gathers AI–nanorobot coordination, bioelectric and quantum sensing, philosophical and physical dual-track validation, bounded autonomous platforms, and open negative-case reconstruction. The purpose is not to announce that a new acupuncture mechanism has been confirmed. It is to design a research archive in which every ambitious model comes with a stronger rival, a declared uncertainty and a route to refusal. A well-matched classical baseline may defeat a quantum-labelled architecture. A thermal or electrode artifact may account for a proposed biofield. Two cultural readers may agree about an ancient text yet disagree about the physical proxy that should test its modern interpretation. A capable control system must still stop when a human revokes permission. Finally, a striking result should remain provisional until a different laboratory can reconstruct its adverse cases and explain why the result might be false. The family is situated in Eastern philosophical traditions as intellectual history and an ethics of balance and responsibility, while empirical claims are restricted to independently observable measurements. All diagrams, surfaces and numerical grids in this volume are synthetic and prospective. There is no clinical intervention, biological proof, medical-device validation, confirmed remote effect or established new field. The volume offers thirty inherited candidate relationships, forty-two open numerical models, eighty-two staged chapter investigations, two hundred research doors, and thirty-three successor prototype sketches. Its deepest ambition is methodological: to make a future researcher more capable of falsifying it than the original author could have been. summary: INTEGRATED INTELLIGENT ACUPUNCTURE NANO-QUANTUM RESEARCH AT THE LIMIT F196–F200 · STARLI · White Rainbow Era · Research Working Edition v1.0 Prospective research essence | Nonclinical | Synthetic mathematical models At the end of forty integrated families, the central question changes. How can a research civilization connect five kinds of evidence while preserving the right to disagree? Family 40 gathers AI–nanorobot coordination, bioelectric and quantum sensing, philosophical and physical dual-track validation, bounded autonomous platforms, and open negative-case reconstruction. The purpose is not to announce that a new acupuncture mechanism has been confirmed. It is to design a research archive in which every ambitious model comes with a stronger rival, a declared uncertainty and a route to refusal. A well-matched classical baseline may defeat a quantum-labelled architecture. A thermal or electrode artifact may account for a proposed biofield. Two cultural readers may agree about an ancient text yet disagree about the physical proxy that should test its modern interpretation. A capable control system must still stop when a human revokes permission. Finally, a striking result should remain provisional until a different laboratory can reconstruct its adverse cases and explain why the result might be false. The family is situated in Eastern philosophical traditions as intellectual history and an ethics of balance and responsibility, while empirical claims are restricted to independently observable measurements. All diagrams, surfaces and numerical grids in this volume are synthetic and prospective. There is no clinical intervention, biological proof, medical-device validation, confirmed remote effect or established new field. The volume offers thirty inherited candidate relationships, forty-two open numerical models, eighty-two staged chapter investigations, two hundred research doors, and thirty-three successor prototype sketches. Its deepest ambition is methodological: to make a future researcher more capable of falsifying it than the original author could have been. summary: INTEGRATED INTELLIGENT ACUPUNCTURE NANO-QUANTUM RESEARCH AT THE LIMIT F196–F200 · STARLI · White Rainbow Era · Research Working Edition v1.0 Prospective research essence | Nonclinical | Synthetic mathematical models At the end of forty integrated families, the central question changes. How can a research civilization connect five kinds of evidence while preserving the right to disagree? Family 40 gathers AI–nanorobot coordination, bioelectric and quantum sensing, philosophical and physical dual-track validation, bounded autonomous platforms, and open negative-case reconstruction. The purpose is not to announce that a new acupuncture mechanism has been confirmed. It is to design a research archive in which every ambitious model comes with a stronger rival, a declared uncertainty and a route to refusal. A well-matched classical baseline may defeat a quantum-labelled architecture. A thermal or electrode artifact may account for a proposed biofield. Two cultural readers may agree about an ancient text yet disagree about the physical proxy that should test its modern interpretation. A capable control system must still stop when a human revokes permission. Finally, a striking result should remain provisional until a different laboratory can reconstruct its adverse cases and explain why the result might be false. The family is situated in Eastern philosophical traditions as intellectual history and an ethics of balance and responsibility, while empirical claims are restricted to independently observable measurements. All diagrams, surfaces and numerical grids in this volume are synthetic and prospective. There is no clinical intervention, biological proof, medical-device validation, confirmed remote effect or established new field. The volume offers thirty inherited candidate relationships, forty-two open numerical models, eighty-two staged chapter investigations, two hundred research doors, and thirty-three successor prototype sketches. Its deepest ambition is methodological: to make a future researcher more capable of falsifying it than the original author could have been. summary: INTEGRATED INTELLIGENT ACUPUNCTURE NANO-QUANTUM RESEARCH AT THE LIMIT F196–F200 · STARLI · White Rainbow Era · Research Working Edition v1.0 Prospective research essence | Nonclinical | Synthetic mathematical models At the end of forty integrated families, the central question changes. How can a research civilization connect five kinds of evidence while preserving the right to disagree? Family 40 gathers AI–nanorobot coordination, bioelectric and quantum sensing, philosophical and physical dual-track validation, bounded autonomous platforms, and open negative-case reconstruction. The purpose is not to announce that a new acupuncture mechanism has been confirmed. It is to design a research archive in which every ambitious model comes with a stronger rival, a declared uncertainty and a route to refusal. A well-matched classical baseline may defeat a quantum-labelled architecture. A thermal or electrode artifact may account for a proposed biofield. Two cultural readers may agree about an ancient text yet disagree about the physical proxy that should test its modern interpretation. A capable control system must still stop when a human revokes permission. Finally, a striking result should remain provisional until a different laboratory can reconstruct its adverse cases and explain why the result might be false. The family is situated in Eastern philosophical traditions as intellectual history and an ethics of balance and responsibility, while empirical claims are restricted to independently observable measurements. All diagrams, surfaces and numerical grids in this volume are synthetic and prospective. There is no clinical intervention, biological proof, medical-device validation, confirmed remote effect or established new field. The volume offers thirty inherited candidate relationships, forty-two open numerical models, eighty-two staged chapter investigations, two hundred research doors, and thirty-three successor prototype sketches. Its deepest ambition is methodological: to make a future researcher more capable of falsifying it than the original author could have been. summary: INTEGRATED INTELLIGENT ACUPUNCTURE NANO-QUANTUM RESEARCH AT THE LIMIT F196–F200 · STARLI · White Rainbow Era · Research Working Edition v1.0 Prospective research essence | Nonclinical | Synthetic mathematical models At the end of forty integrated families, the central question changes. How can a research civilization connect five kinds of evidence while preserving the right to disagree? Family 40 gathers AI–nanorobot coordination, bioelectric and quantum sensing, philosophical and physical dual-track validation, bounded autonomous platforms, and open negative-case reconstruction. The purpose is not to announce that a new acupuncture mechanism has been confirmed. It is to design a research archive in which every ambitious model comes with a stronger rival, a declared uncertainty and a route to refusal. A well-matched classical baseline may defeat a quantum-labelled architecture. A thermal or electrode artifact may account for a proposed biofield. Two cultural readers may agree about an ancient text yet disagree about the physical proxy that should test its modern interpretation. A capable control system must still stop when a human revokes permission. Finally, a striking result should remain provisional until a different laboratory can reconstruct its adverse cases and explain why the result might be false. The family is situated in Eastern philosophical traditions as intellectual history and an ethics of balance and responsibility, while empirical claims are restricted to independently observable measurements. All diagrams, surfaces and numerical grids in this volume are synthetic and prospective. There is no clinical intervention, biological proof, medical-device validation, confirmed remote effect or established new field. The volume offers thirty inherited candidate relationships, forty-two open numerical models, eighty-two staged chapter investigations, two hundred research doors, and thirty-three successor prototype sketches. Its deepest ambition is methodological: to make a future researcher more capable of falsifying it than the original author could have been. summary: INTEGRATED INTELLIGENT ACUPUNCTURE NANO-QUANTUM RESEARCH AT THE LIMIT F196–F200 · STARLI · White Rainbow Era · Research Working Edition v1.0 Prospective research essence | Nonclinical | Synthetic mathematical models At the end of forty integrated families, the central question changes. How can a research civilization connect five kinds of evidence while preserving the right to disagree? Family 40 gathers AI–nanorobot coordination, bioelectric and quantum sensing, philosophical and physical dual-track validation, bounded autonomous platforms, and open negative-case reconstruction. The purpose is not to announce that a new acupuncture mechanism has been confirmed. It is to design a research archive in which every ambitious model comes with a stronger rival, a declared uncertainty and a route to refusal. A well-matched classical baseline may defeat a quantum-labelled architecture. A thermal or electrode artifact may account for a proposed biofield. Two cultural readers may agree about an ancient text yet disagree about the physical proxy that should test its modern interpretation. A capable control system must still stop when a human revokes permission. Finally, a striking result should remain provisional until a different laboratory can reconstruct its adverse cases and explain why the result might be false. The family is situated in Eastern philosophical traditions as intellectual history and an ethics of balance and responsibility, while empirical claims are restricted to independently observable measurements. All diagrams, surfaces and numerical grids in this volume are synthetic and prospective. There is no clinical intervention, biological proof, medical-device validation, confirmed remote effect or established new field. The volume offers thirty inherited candidate relationships, forty-two open numerical models, eighty-two staged chapter investigations, two hundred research doors, and thirty-three successor prototype sketches. Its deepest ambition is methodological: to make a future researcher more capable of falsifying it than the original author could have been. summary: INTEGRATED INTELLIGENT ACUPUNCTURE NANO-QUANTUM RESEARCH AT THE LIMIT F196–F200 · STARLI · White Rainbow Era · Research Working Edition v1.0 Prospective research essence | Nonclinical | Synthetic mathematical models At the end of forty integrated families, the central question changes. How can a research civilization connect five kinds of evidence while preserving the right to disagree? Family 40 gathers AI–nanorobot coordination, bioelectric and quantum sensing, philosophical and physical dual-track validation, bounded autonomous platforms, and open negative-case reconstruction. The purpose is not to announce that a new acupuncture mechanism has been confirmed. It is to design a research archive in which every ambitious model comes with a stronger rival, a declared uncertainty and a route to refusal. A well-matched classical baseline may defeat a quantum-labelled architecture. A thermal or electrode artifact may account for a proposed biofield. Two cultural readers may agree about an ancient text yet disagree about the physical proxy that should test its modern interpretation. A capable control system must still stop when a human revokes permission. Finally, a striking result should remain provisional until a different laboratory can reconstruct its adverse cases and explain why the result might be false. The family is situated in Eastern philosophical traditions as intellectual history and an ethics of balance and responsibility, while empirical claims are restricted to independently observable measurements. All diagrams, surfaces and numerical grids in this volume are synthetic and prospective. There is no clinical intervention, biological proof, medical-device validation, confirmed remote effect or established new field. The volume offers thirty inherited candidate relationships, forty-two open numerical models, eighty-two staged chapter investigations, two hundred research doors, and thirty-three successor prototype sketches. Its deepest ambition is methodological: to make a future researcher more capable of falsifying it than the original author could have been. summary: INTEGRATED INTELLIGENT ACUPUNCTURE NANO-QUANTUM RESEARCH AT THE LIMIT F196–F200 · STARLI · White Rainbow Era · Research Working Edition v1.0 Prospective research essence | Nonclinical | Synthetic mathematical models At the end of forty integrated families, the central question changes. How can a research civilization connect five kinds of evidence while preserving the right to disagree? Family 40 gathers AI–nanorobot coordination, bioelectric and quantum sensing, philosophical and physical dual-track validation, bounded autonomous platforms, and open negative-case reconstruction. The purpose is not to announce that a new acupuncture mechanism has been confirmed. It is to design a research archive in which every ambitious model comes with a stronger rival, a declared uncertainty and a route to refusal. A well-matched classical baseline may defeat a quantum-labelled architecture. A thermal or electrode artifact may account for a proposed biofield. Two cultural readers may agree about an ancient text yet disagree about the physical proxy that should test its modern interpretation. A capable control system must still stop when a human revokes permission. Finally, a striking result should remain provisional until a different laboratory can reconstruct its adverse cases and explain why the result might be false. The family is situated in Eastern philosophical traditions as intellectual history and an ethics of balance and responsibility, while empirical claims are restricted to independently observable measurements. All diagrams, surfaces and numerical grids in this volume are synthetic and prospective. There is no clinical intervention, biological proof, medical-device validation, confirmed remote effect or established new field. The volume offers thirty inherited candidate relationships, forty-two open numerical models, eighty-two staged chapter investigations, two hundred research doors, and thirty-three successor prototype sketches. Its deepest ambition is methodological: to make a future researcher more capable of falsifying it than the original author could have been. summary: INTEGRATED INTELLIGENT ACUPUNCTURE NANO-QUANTUM RESEARCH AT THE LIMIT F196–F200 · STARLI · White Rainbow Era · Research Working Edition v1.0 Prospective research essence | Nonclinical | Synthetic mathematical models At the end of forty integrated families, the central question changes. How can a research civilization connect five kinds of evidence while preserving the right to disagree? Family 40 gathers AI–nanorobot coordination, bioelectric and quantum sensing, philosophical and physical dual-track validation, bounded autonomous platforms, and open negative-case reconstruction. The purpose is not to announce that a new acupuncture mechanism has been confirmed. It is to design a research archive in which every ambitious model comes with a stronger rival, a declared uncertainty and a route to refusal. A well-matched classical baseline may defeat a quantum-labelled architecture. A thermal or electrode artifact may account for a proposed biofield. Two cultural readers may agree about an ancient text yet disagree about the physical proxy that should test its modern interpretation. A capable control system must still stop when a human revokes permission. Finally, a striking result should remain provisional until a different laboratory can reconstruct its adverse cases and explain why the result might be false. The family is situated in Eastern philosophical traditions as intellectual history and an ethics of balance and responsibility, while empirical claims are restricted to independently observable measurements. All diagrams, surfaces and numerical grids in this volume are synthetic and prospective. There is no clinical intervention, biological proof, medical-device validation, confirmed remote effect or established new field. The volume offers thirty inherited candidate relationships, forty-two open numerical models, eighty-two staged chapter investigations, two hundred research doors, and thirty-three successor prototype sketches. Its deepest ambition is methodological: to make a future researcher more capable of falsifying it than the original author could have been. summary: INTEGRATED INTELLIGENT ACUPUNCTURE NANO-QUANTUM RESEARCH AT THE LIMIT F196–F200 · STARLI · White Rainbow Era · Research Working Edition v1.0 Prospective research essence | Nonclinical | Synthetic mathematical models At the end of forty integrated families, the central question changes. How can a research civilization connect five kinds of evidence while preserving the right to disagree? Family 40 gathers AI–nanorobot coordination, bioelectric and quantum sensing, philosophical and physical dual-track validation, bounded autonomous platforms, and open negative-case reconstruction. The purpose is not to announce that a new acupuncture mechanism has been confirmed. It is to design a research archive in which every ambitious model comes with a stronger rival, a declared uncertainty and a route to refusal. A well-matched classical baseline may defeat a quantum-labelled architecture. A thermal or electrode artifact may account for a proposed biofield. Two cultural readers may agree about an ancient text yet disagree about the physical proxy that should test its modern interpretation. A capable control system must still stop when a human revokes permission. Finally, a striking result should remain provisional until a different laboratory can reconstruct its adverse cases and explain why the result might be false. The family is situated in Eastern philosophical traditions as intellectual history and an ethics of balance and responsibility, while empirical claims are restricted to independently observable measurements. All diagrams, surfaces and numerical grids in this volume are synthetic and prospective. There is no clinical intervention, biological proof, medical-device validation, confirmed remote effect or established new field. The volume offers thirty inherited candidate relationships, forty-two open numerical models, eighty-two staged chapter investigations, two hundred research doors, and thirty-three successor prototype sketches. Its deepest ambition is methodological: to make a future researcher more capable of falsifying it than the original author could have been. summary: INTEGRATED INTELLIGENT ACUPUNCTURE NANO-QUANTUM RESEARCH AT THE LIMIT F196–F200 · STARLI · White Rainbow Era · Research Working Edition v1.0 Prospective research essence | Nonclinical | Synthetic mathematical models At the end of forty integrated families, the central question changes. How can a research civilization connect five kinds of evidence while preserving the right to disagree? Family 40 gathers AI–nanorobot coordination, bioelectric and quantum sensing, philosophical and physical dual-track validation, bounded autonomous platforms, and open negative-case reconstruction. The purpose is not to announce that a new acupuncture mechanism has been confirmed. It is to design a research archive in which every ambitious model comes with a stronger rival, a declared uncertainty and a route to refusal. A well-matched classical baseline may defeat a quantum-labelled architecture. A thermal or electrode artifact may account for a proposed biofield. Two cultural readers may agree about an ancient text yet disagree about the physical proxy that should test its modern interpretation. A capable control system must still stop when a human revokes permission. Finally, a striking result should remain provisional until a different laboratory can reconstruct its adverse cases and explain why the result might be false. The family is situated in Eastern philosophical traditions as intellectual history and an ethics of balance and responsibility, while empirical claims are restricted to independently observable measurements. All diagrams, surfaces and numerical grids in this volume are synthetic and prospective. There is no clinical intervention, biological proof, medical-device validation, confirmed remote effect or established new field. The volume offers thirty inherited candidate relationships, forty-two open numerical models, eighty-two staged chapter investigations, two hundred research doors, and thirty-three successor prototype sketches. Its deepest ambition is methodological: to make a future researcher more capable of falsifying it than the original author could have been. A well-matched classical baseline may defeat a quantum-labelled architecture. A thermal or electrode artifact may account for a proposed biofield. Two cultural readers may agree about an ancient text yet disagree about the physical proxy that should test its modern interpretation. A capable control system must still stop when a human revokes permission. summary: Printing a floating-point number and reading it back should recover its bits. We find exactly 626,159 positive finite binary64 values whose shortest CPython spelling SQLite 3.54.1 reads as a neighbor. These failures collapse disjoint adjacent pairs. SQLite's default writer reverses 5,084 of those pairs. On each, SQLite reads its own text back to the stored value, while correct rounding gives its neighbor. We count them by locating incorrect midpoint decisions and identifying which decimals CPython can print. A repair adds 104 bytes to SQLite's power table and gives correct rounding for every 64-bit coefficient passed to the converter. Compiled versions with wide and portable multiplication agreed with exact rounding in 2,402,440 selected cases. A separate limit arises before conversion. Two 20-digit decimals can require different answers even when the scanner retains the same prefix and discards a nonzero digit from both. We determine exactly how many binary rounding boundaries remain ambiguous as additional decimal digits are retained. An exact suffix comparison and a correction to exponent accumulation give a complete reader for accepted ASCII decimals below the stated length limit. It matched whole-text rounding on 1,296,347 native tests. An x86-64 Linux build on the same Mac reproduced all five native output streams in each of seven cohorts. The complete Linux reader matched the reference on all 55,670 additional public input rows. The released reader misrounded 157 public test spellings. REAL-column import also changed 910 negative zeros to positive zero. SQLite's 18-digit format preserves every finite nonzero value with either reader.

Contains result files, exploratory tables, figures, the analysis notebook (outputs removed) and registered code, the printed output of the later exploratory cells, a ledger comparing every number in the manuscript with the saved results, the specification and predictions for the later exploratory analyses (written before each run), a guide to re-collecting the data, the pre-analysis plan for a prospective test, the written second rating of the 60-word mapping check, Wikimedia page-view data behind the salience index (as a NumPy archive), and a run-order list of every cell. Version 8 supersedes versions 1 to 7: it adds the selection check on the discovery sample and the minimum detectable effect of the prospective plan (Cell 133a) and the reconciliation of Table 8 with Table A16 (Cell 133b), and it cites the prospective-test plan version 4 (doi:10.5281/zenodo.24450089; earlier versions doi:10.5281/zenodo.24443393, doi:10.5281/zenodo.24448264 and doi:10.5281/zenodo.24448367) and the quote logger version 3.2 (doi:10.5281/zenodo.24451715). Row-level Kalshi data, the raw trade cache and the event-metadata cache are not included, because Kalshi's Developer Agreement restricts sharing API data without written authorization; they are listed with SHA-256 hashes in OMITTED_FILES.csv. The Study 1, Study 2B and Study 1b plans and code are deposited separately (DOIs 10.5281/zenodo.24377284, 10.5281/zenodo.24396719, 10.5281/zenodo.24396948, 10.5281/zenodo.24410354, 10.5281/zenodo.24410400 and 10.5281/zenodo.24426046). Zip: repro_package_20261123_013627.zip, built 2026-11-23 01:36 UTC, SHA-256 3737190bfba5430618b7b006e985c639c1b263357da5ac3b6c3b695a53cb52a9. See README.md and REGISTERED_IDENTIFIERS.txt.

summary: This artifact accompanies the poster paper "Evaluating Multi-Agent Incident Response: Baseline Design, Efficiency, and Policy Compliance" by Ebelechukwu Nwafor and Habeeb Olufowobi, accepted at the ACM/SIGAPP Symposium on Applied Computing (SAC '27). The paper asks whether a multi-agent LLM workflow for incident response is more efficient than a single agent, and shows that the answer depends on how the single-agent baseline is built. It evaluates MAN-IDS, a four-role LLM workflow, against single-agent baselines and a deterministic rule in three controlled studies on a Docker test network with Redis and PostgreSQL access scenarios. Contents - The MAN-IDS system and the evaluation harness (runners, scoring, decision protocol). - All prompts, model versions, and settings used in the studies. - The protocol for each study, written before any model calls were made. - Complete run records with full traces for 1,152 scheduled investigations across 64 campaigns:   - Study 1: explicit response policy, Claude Sonnet 5, 384 runs.   - Study 2: detector gating and routing repair, Claude Sonnet 5, 512 runs.   - Study 3: replication with Qwen3-8B on fresh campaigns, 256 runs. - Analysis scripts and their saved outputs, including the stage-timing, format-versus-decision, and comparable-quality re-analyses reported in the paper. - The trace analysis that motivated the routing repair, with the run records of the earlier evaluation it reads. - Detector experiment outputs (splits, predictions, reports) derived from CICIDS2017 and CSE-CIC-IDS2018. - The test-network setup (Docker Compose files, topology, schemas). Reproducing the results No model calls or API keys are needed. Running "python3 reproduce_analyses.py" re-runs the three study analyses from the saved run records and reports whether each result matches the shipped file byte for byte. The README lists the required Python packages and the remaining commands. Notes - Response actions were never executed. All tools are controlled and non-executing. - The public datasets are not redistributed. Only derived splits, predictions, and reports are included. - Run traces contain the absolute file paths of the machines that produced them. - Re-running the model studies would require an Anthropic API key (Studies 1 and 2) or a GPU serving Qwen3-8B (Study 3), plus Docker. License: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0).

summary: This record registers, before any per-origin value was read, a test of how three checkpoint-relief alleles combine at individual budding-yeast replication origins. The data are the eight-genotype factorials of Sheu, Kinney and Stillman (2016, Genome Research 26:315–330), taken from the authors' repository (github.com/jbkinney/14_sheu, commit 026c2ef). The primary test uses the 0.2 M HU, 90-min factorial. The 0.05% MMS factorial serves as an agreement test, and the unperturbed 25-min factorial as a negative control. A triple-mutant HU time course, run in two separate experiments, supplies the HU noise estimate. Product, additive and constrained stochastic-threshold models are compared in a single censored likelihood. Each sample carries its own scale and floor. Three gates come first: a replicate control, an unperturbed null and an information check. A verdict requires agreement across floor treatments, width adjustment, doubled noise and the MMS condition. Every verdict is provisional pending a replicated HU factorial. The design corrects three errors in the earlier Pol α registration (10.5281/zenodo.24450406): a missing scale term, a floor treated as exact, and an ambiguous reference level. Version 2 adds Amendment 1, filed before any per-origin value was read: the condition assignment is confirmed from figure captions and per-sample settings because Supplemental Table 1 is not accessible; floor treatment F1 is recomputed from the repository profiles; and a second HU 90-min replicate gate (set 7 vs set 4) is added. Version 3 deposits the outcome. The registered analysis terminated at Gate 3, the unperturbed negative control: three of four interaction terms exceeded the registered threshold with the checkpoint inactive (mcm4Δ74-174 × dbf4-19A γ = 1.40, 95% CI 0.98–1.85). The registered outcome is uninterpretable, and the HU combination-rule comparison was not performed. Gates 2, 2b and 4 passed. Code and outputs reproduce every reported number from the authors' repository (commit 026c2ef).
title: Prospective registration: combination rules for sld3-38A, dbf4-19A and mcm4Δ74-174 at individual replication origins in the Sheu et al. (2016) factorial

summary: Data and analysis files supporting Salichos et al., Multi-host phylodynamics of hepatitis E virus reveals extensive lineage sharing across humans, wild boar, and swine . The study analysed 436 hepatitis E virus ORF2 sequences from humans, wild boar, swine and camels, together with 49 ICTV subtype reference genomes. Subtypes were reassigned de novo by phylogenetic placement, and time-calibrated coalescent and birth–death skyline analyses were run for 13 subtype- and host-specific datasets, followed by a discrete-trait analysis of host transitions among HEV-3 lineages. This deposit contains the 411 bp alignment and per-analysis alignments with sampling dates, sequence metadata after filtering and deduplication, BEAST v2.7.7 XML input files, parameter log files, the annotated maximum clade credibility and maximum-likelihood trees shown in the figures, and the scripts used for the temporal-signal testing, the host and subtype rate comparison, and Figures 2 and 4. All sequences are publicly available in GenBank; accession numbers are listed in alignments/metadata.tsv . Results tables are published with the article and are not duplicated here. See README.md for the full contents. Version 2 adds three analyses, in HEV_round2_additions.tgz. All version 1 files are unchanged. prior_sens/ — Sensitivity of the becoming-uninfectious rate (δ) to its prior. Four datasets (HEV-3f all hosts, HEV-3f swine, HEV-3c human, HEV-3a wild boar) re-analysed under three alternative lognormal priors on δ, alongside the prior used in the main analysis: twelve BEAST v2.7.7 input files, the twelve parameter logs of 100 million states each, the four baseline logs, and a summary table of prior and posterior δ. subtype_bssvs/ — The discrete-trait host-transition analysis repeated within individual HEV-3 subtypes, for the three subtypes containing all three host states with more than four sequences per host: HEV-3f (n = 131), HEV-3c (n = 82) and HEV-3e (n = 48). Three input files, two independent chains of 200 million states per subtype, and a summary table of posterior inclusion probabilities, Bayes factors and transition rates for all six pathways. window_unconstrained/ — The 411 bp ORF2 window tree re-estimated without the whole-genome backbone constraint, used to check that the subtype assignments do not depend on it. IQ-TREE v3.1.4 outputs and the resulting assignments. scripts/make_figure4_bssvs.py generates Figure 4 and supersedes scripts/Figure4_BSSVS.py from version 1, which implemented an earlier treatment of the rate indicators.
title: Multi-host phylodynamics of hepatitis E virus reveals extensive lineage sharing across humans, wild boar, and swine

summary: Data and analysis files supporting Salichos et al., Multi-host phylodynamics of hepatitis E virus reveals extensive lineage sharing across humans, wild boar, and swine . The study analysed 436 hepatitis E virus ORF2 sequences from humans, wild boar, swine and camels, together with 49 ICTV subtype reference genomes. Subtypes were reassigned de novo by phylogenetic placement, and time-calibrated coalescent and birth–death skyline analyses were run for 13 subtype- and host-specific datasets, followed by a discrete-trait analysis of host transitions among HEV-3 lineages. This deposit contains the 411 bp alignment and per-analysis alignments with sampling dates, sequence metadata after filtering and deduplication, BEAST v2.7.7 XML input files, parameter log files, the annotated maximum clade credibility and maximum-likelihood trees shown in the figures, and the scripts used for the temporal-signal testing, the host and subtype rate comparison, and Figures 2 and 4. All sequences are publicly available in GenBank; accession numbers are listed in alignments/metadata.tsv . Results tables are published with the article and are not duplicated here. See README.md for the full contents. Version 2 adds three analyses, in HEV_round2_additions.tgz. All version 1 files are unchanged. prior_sens/ — Sensitivity of the becoming-uninfectious rate (δ) to its prior. Four datasets (HEV-3f all hosts, HEV-3f swine, HEV-3c human, HEV-3a wild boar) re-analysed under three alternative lognormal priors on δ, alongside the prior used in the main analysis: twelve BEAST v2.7.7 input files, the twelve parameter logs of 100 million states each, the four baseline logs, and a summary table of prior and posterior δ. subtype_bssvs/ — The discrete-trait host-transition analysis repeated within individual HEV-3 subtypes, for the three subtypes containing all three host states with more than four sequences per host: HEV-3f (n = 131), HEV-3c (n = 82) and HEV-3e (n = 48). Three input files, two independent chains of 200 million states per subtype, and a summary table of posterior inclusion probabilities, Bayes factors and transition rates for all six pathways. window_unconstrained/ — The 411 bp ORF2 window tree re-estimated without the whole-genome backbone constraint, used to check that the subtype assignments do not depend on it. IQ-TREE v3.1.4 outputs and the resulting assignments. scripts/make_figure4_bssvs.py generates Figure 4 and supersedes scripts/Figure4_BSSVS.py from version 1, which implemented an earlier treatment of the rate indicators.

summary: This record contains the code, the processed input data and the results of every run of a benchmark study on the day-ahead and rolling-horizon scheduling of building energy systems with photovoltaics (PV), photovoltaic-thermal (PVT) collectors, a battery, a heat pump and a thermal storage tank.   The study compares three quantum-inspired metaheuristics (quantum-inspired evolutionary algorithm, quantum-behaved particle swarm optimisation, simulated quantum annealing) with their classical counterparts (genetic algorithm, particle swarm optimisation, simulated annealing), with general-purpose optimisers (differential evolution, L-SHADE, sep-CMA-ES, jSO, Gaussian QPSO, real-coded QEA, coordinate pattern search) and with mixed-integer linear programming (an exact MILP for the linear instances, a naive linearisation, a piecewise-linear MILP and its three-band and scenario-based forms). All optimisers receive the same number of objective-function evaluations and are tuned with one protocol.   Experiments - 21 synthetic day-ahead instances with 24 to 864 decision variables, 30 runs per algorithm and instance, evaluation budgets of 5,000, 20,000 and 100,000 - 1,311 data-driven day-ahead instances in three climates (typical-meteorological-year weather, measured electrical loads) - component ablations, budgets proportional to the number of variables, settings tuned at 864 variables - warm starts from the schedule of the piecewise-linear MILP - one year of rolling-horizon operation with 19 controllers, with and without a weekly demand charge, and three shorter variants (perfect forecasts, a second forecast-error model, random initialisation at every step)   Contents (143 files, 44 MB compressed) - qio_ies/: simulator of the energy system (numba), optimisers, MILP models, rolling-horizon operation - scripts/: one script per experiment, the statistical analysis, and the scripts that write the tables and figures - data/: processed measured load series - results/: output of every run (CSV, NPZ, JSON), reference costs and analysis tables - README.md: layout, commands and requirements   Reproduction The analysis tables and the tables and figures of the accompanying article can be regenerated from the stored run results with the analysis, table and figure scripts listed in README.md. The experiments themselves can be repeated with the run scripts. Metaheuristic runs are deterministic for a given seed. Extract the archive with the file times preserved.   Requirements Python 3.11 with numpy, scipy (HiGHS), numba, pandas, joblib, matplotlib and pvlib. The results were produced with Python 3.11.9, numpy 2.4.6, scipy 1.17.1, numba 0.66.0, pandas 3.0.3, matplotlib 3.11.0, joblib 1.5.3 and pvlib 0.15.2.   Data sources The weather records are the typical-meteorological-year files distributed with pvlib. The measured loads are derived from the UCI data set ElectricityLoadDiagrams20112014 (https://doi.org/10.24432/C58C86).

summary: This record contains the code, the processed input data and the results of every run of a benchmark study on the day-ahead and rolling-horizon scheduling of building energy systems with photovoltaics (PV), photovoltaic-thermal (PVT) collectors, a battery, a heat pump and a thermal storage tank.   The study compares three quantum-inspired metaheuristics (quantum-inspired evolutionary algorithm, quantum-behaved particle swarm optimisation, simulated quantum annealing) with their classical counterparts (genetic algorithm, particle swarm optimisation, simulated annealing), with general-purpose optimisers (differential evolution, L-SHADE, sep-CMA-ES, jSO, Gaussian QPSO, real-coded QEA, coordinate pattern search) and with mixed-integer linear programming (an exact MILP for the linear instances, a naive linearisation, a piecewise-linear MILP and its three-band and scenario-based forms). All optimisers receive the same number of objective-function evaluations and are tuned with one protocol.   Experiments - 21 synthetic day-ahead instances with 24 to 864 decision variables, 30 runs per algorithm and instance, evaluation budgets of 5,000, 20,000 and 100,000 - 1,311 data-driven day-ahead instances in three climates (typical-meteorological-year weather, measured electrical loads) - component ablations, budgets proportional to the number of variables, settings tuned at 864 variables - warm starts from the schedule of the piecewise-linear MILP - one year of rolling-horizon operation with 19 controllers, with and without a weekly demand charge, and three shorter variants (perfect forecasts, a second forecast-error model, random initialisation at every step)   Contents (143 files, 44 MB compressed) - qio_ies/: simulator of the energy system (numba), optimisers, MILP models, rolling-horizon operation - scripts/: one script per experiment, the statistical analysis, and the scripts that write the tables and figures - data/: processed measured load series - results/: output of every run (CSV, NPZ, JSON), reference costs and analysis tables - README.md: layout, commands and requirements   Reproduction The analysis tables and the tables and figures of the accompanying article can be regenerated from the stored run results with the analysis, table and figure scripts listed in README.md. The experiments themselves can be repeated with the run scripts. Metaheuristic runs are deterministic for a given seed. Extract the archive with the file times preserved.   Requirements Python 3.11 with numpy, scipy (HiGHS), numba, pandas, joblib, matplotlib and pvlib. The results were produced with Python 3.11.9, numpy 2.4.6, scipy 1.17.1, numba 0.66.0, pandas 3.0.3, matplotlib 3.11.0, joblib 1.5.3 and pvlib 0.15.2.   Data sources The weather records are the typical-meteorological-year files distributed with pvlib. The measured loads are derived from the UCI data set ElectricityLoadDiagrams20112014 (https://doi.org/10.24432/C58C86).
